input.quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
input.rationale: Section 21 meets the preferred position. The cap is expressly mutual and set at the greater of (a) Fees paid or payable by Customer in the twelve months preceding the event and (b) USD 1,000,000; § 21.2 excludes indirect/consequential damages mutually (and helpfully confirms data-restoration, replacement-service, notification and incident-response costs are direct damages); and § 21.3 defines "Excluded Claims" to place confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, and infringement of the other Party's IP outside both the cap and the damages exclusion. § 21.3 also confirms Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is not "damages" and § 21.4 preserves liabilities that cannot lawfully be limited. "Fees" (§ 1.5) is a meaningful base covering subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the cap is not illusory; the only minor gap is that Fees exclude a one-time implementation charge, which we note but do not redline. No competing or one-sided liability language appears elsewhere (§ 18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities). The § 7.6 liquidated-damages and indemnity points are addressed under their own rules and are not double-flagged here.
